The image shows a recent Omega Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch with a black "step dial"... Actually it looks like a Hesalite or sapphire version. Key details: "OMEGA Speedmaster PROFESSIONAL" with "PROFESSIONAL" in red? No — the logo appears in white/red? Let me look: "Speedmaster Professional" text under the Omega logo. The hands are white baton with lollipop? Actually the subdial hands are white. The bracelet is a 5-link... Actually the bracelet appears to be a 5-row (three-row plus?) It looks like a flattened "Nixon"? Hmm, but it seems the bracelet has 5 links across, similar to... Hmm, older Speedmasters have 3-link bracelets. This one shows multiple narrow rows — possibly a 5-link (like the Omega 1479 or a "Speedmaster 57" style?). Actually the modern Speedmaster Professional 3861 bracelet (ref 020STZ011413?) has 3 links. Wait, the photo shows a bracelet with several parallel rows — maybe 5 links, reminiscent of the vintage-style "flat link" 1479 bracelet? Hmm.

Actually, the newer 2021+ Moonwatch bracelets are 3-link with polished center? No, they have a 5-link?? The new 3861 bracelet has 3 links with... Hmm, the 2021 Moonwatch bracelet has a "flat link" appearance, with 3 links but the outer links narrow? It's described as a new bracelet with 5 rows? Let me recall: The Speedmaster Professional 3861 (2021) — bracelet ref 020STZ012469, three-link brushed with polished inner? Actually I believe it's a 3-link design derived from the vintage 1479.

Hmm, the photo shows what appears to be multiple thin links, maybe due to the angle. The crystal edge shows hesalite-like? Hard to tell. The dial appears to have a step (the main dial is recessed) which suggests sapphire version 310.30.42.50.01.002 (hesalite) vs .002 sapphire? Actually:
- 310.30.42.50.01.001 — hesalite, steel bracelet
- 310.30.42.50.01.002 — sapphire, steel bracelet

The sapphire version has a "step dial" (milled step). The hesalite version has a flat dial with printed logo? Actually: hesalite version has applied logo? No — the hesalite version has a printed Ω logo and painted... Hmm. In the 2021 Moonwatch:
- Hesalite: printed Omega logo, no step dial... Actually reversed: The sapphire version (310.30.42.50.01.002) has an applied metal Omega logo and a step dial. The hesalite (310.30.42.50.01.001) has a printed logo and flat dial.

Also, the "Professional" text: on the hesalite it's white; on the sapphire? Hmm.

In this photo, the Omega logo looks applied (raised), and there's a step in the dial (visible ring around the center). Also the "Speedmaster Professional" appears in white script. The sapphire version typically has the "Ω" applied and "Speedmaster" in white with "PROFESSIONAL" in orange? No, that's the Speedy Tuesday? Hmm. Actually there's a version with red "Speedmaster" script? The 2021 sapphire has white.

There's also the 310.30.42.50.01.002 with a sapphire crystal, polished... Hmm, the case in the photo appears to have polished lugs? Hard to tell.

Another candidate: the Omega Speedmaster Professional "Apollo 11" 50th? No.

Given the applied logo and step dial, I'd go with 310.30.42.50.01.002 (sapphire sandwich). Confidence maybe 0.35.

Let me think about the bracelet: the sapphire sandwich 3861 came on bracelet 020STZ012469? Hmm. Actually reference for the sapphire on steel bracelet is 310.30.42.50.01.002. Yes.

Movement: automatic? No — the Moonwatch Professional is manual-winding (caliber 3861). So movement: manual.

Case material: stainless-steel. Bracelet: metal.

Brand: Omega. Model family: Speedmaster Professional Moonwatch.

Confidence: ~0.35.

Hmm, but is the dial step visible? In the photo, there's a visible circular ridge around the dial near the edges — typical of the step dial in the sapphire version. Yes.
